- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 2220-2233 (the new FIRST_ISSUE_BODY lineage extraction), interacting with scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4862 and scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:63-67
  Problem: The parent-metadata extraction propagates the literal sentinel `(default branch)` as if it were a real branch name. When an orchestrator project runs default-branch-only (no integration branch), `create_security_pass_fix_issue` writes `- Integration branch: \`(default branch)\`` into the fix issue body (orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4862). The judge's new regex `([^`\n]+?)` strips the backticks and captures `(default branch)`, so the follow-up issue is created with `- Integration branch: (default branch)`. On the follow-up's plan/implement run, `resolve_integration_ref.sh` extracts that value, calls `branch_exists "(default branch)"`, gets a 404, emits `::error::Integration branch '(default branch)' declared in child issue #N does not exist.` and returns 1 — a hard, non-self-healing failure on every subsequent plan/implement attempt for that follow-up. Before this diff the follow-up carried no Integration branch line at all and resolved cleanly to the default branch, so this is a regression introduced by the lineage propagation for exactly the project shape the parent-metadata source was meant to serve.
  Why it fails at runtime: follow-up issues created from default-branch-only projects (security-pass fix issues, or any managed issue whose metadata carries the `(default branch)` sentinel) enter a permanent plan/implement error loop instead of resolving to the default branch.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh
  Line or code reference: line 2234 (`[[ "${PR_BASE_REF:-}" =~ ^orchestrator/project-([0-9]+)$ ]]`)
  Problem: The base-branch fallback hardcodes the `orchestrator/project-` prefix, but the integration-branch naming is operator-configurable via `ORCH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH_PATTERN` (README, default `^orchestrator/project-`). On a repo that overrode the pattern, the fallback derivation silently never fires. The parent-metadata source still covers most orchestrator-managed cases, so this is a consistency gap in the heuristic fallback rather than a failure on default configuration.
  Why it fails at runtime: with a custom integration branch pattern, a parent issue lacking metadata (the binance-blessings#288 shape this fallback exists for) produces a follow-up that again resolves to the default branch — the exact defect this PR fixes — with no logged indication that the pattern mismatch was the cause.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
